meaning.en: Worth as little as a feather; said of a death or thing that has no value (the opposite of 重于泰山).
meaning.zh: 比鸿雁的羽毛还轻，形容死得毫无价值或事物微不足道。

equivalents: of no more weight than a feather

examples.zh: 为了私利而死，轻于鸿毛。
examples.en: To die for private gain is to die in vain.

examples.zh: 人固有一死，死有重于泰山，有轻于鸿毛。
examples.en: Everyone must die, some deaths weigh more than Mount Tai and some less than a feather.

story.en: Sima Qian wrote that though death comes to all, one death may be weightier than Mount Tai and another lighter than a goose feather, depending on the cause.
story.zh: “人固有一死，死有重于泰山，或轻于鸿毛，用之所趋异也。”

usage.en: Usually paired with 重于泰山: 死有重于泰山，有轻于鸿毛. Note 轻如鸿毛 is a variant.
usage.zh: 常与“重于泰山”对举。

meaning.en: Pleasant, enjoyable things and occasions.
meaning.zh: 令人心情愉快的美好事情。

examples.zh: 良辰美景，赏心乐事，难得一聚。
examples.en: A fine day, lovely scenery, delightful company; such gatherings are rare.

examples.zh: 读书品茶是他最大的赏心乐事。
examples.en: Reading and sipping tea are his greatest pleasures.

origin.source: 谢灵运《拟魏太子邺中集诗序》

story.en: Xie Lingyun wrote that fine days, beautiful scenes, delighted hearts and joyful occasions (良辰、美景、赏心、乐事) are hard to have all together.
story.zh: “天下良辰、美景、赏心、乐事，四者难并。”

date.zh: 东晋末至南朝宋初 · 5世纪初
date.en: late Eastern Jin to early Liu Song, early 5th c.

usage.en: Positive, slightly literary; often with 良辰美景. Note 赏 is shǎng.
usage.zh: 褒义，书面语，常与“良辰美景”并用。

meaning.en: Stern in appearance but weak and timid within: a bluff.
meaning.zh: 外表强硬，内心怯懦。

examples.zh: 他看上去凶巴巴，其实色厉内荏。
examples.en: He looks fierce, but is really a coward inside.

examples.zh: 对付色厉内荏的对手，要敢于亮剑。
examples.en: Against an opponent who is all bluster, you must dare to stand firm.

story.en: Confucius: one who is stern in countenance but weak within is like a petty thief who burrows through walls.
story.zh: 子曰：“色厉而内荏，譬诸小人，其犹穿窬之盗也与？”

usage.en: Derogatory; 荏 is read rěn, not rèn. Often of bullies and states posing as strong.
usage.zh: 贬义；“荏”读 rěn，常指虚张声势的人或国家。

synonyms: 一切反动派都是纸老虎

meaning.en: A grand and abundant display, of works, collections or exhibits.
meaning.zh: 形容事物丰富盛大，蔚为壮观，多指文章、作品、展品。

examples.zh: 这个展览汇集了千件珍品，洋洋大观。
examples.en: The exhibition brings together a thousand treasures, a magnificent array.

examples.zh: 他的文集有三十卷，洋洋大观。
examples.en: His collected works run to thirty volumes, a vast and impressive body.

usage.en: Praise for abundance, mostly of written works and collections; formal. Often confused with 洋洋洒洒.
usage.zh: 褒义，多形容文集、展品之多；常与“洋洋洒洒”相混。

meaning.en: To go back on one's word for one's own benefit.
meaning.zh: 说话不算数，只图自己占便宜。

equivalents: go back on one's word for gain

examples.zh: 他一再食言而肥，没人再信他。
examples.en: He kept breaking promises to his advantage, and nobody trusts him now.

examples.zh: 做生意要讲信用，不能食言而肥。
examples.en: In business you must honour your word, not break it for profit.

story.en: The Duke of Lu said Meng Wubo spoke much 'eating his words' and thus grew fat (食言多矣，能无肥乎).
story.zh: 孟武伯说话不算数，鲁哀公讽刺：“是食言多矣，能无肥乎？”

usage.en: Derogatory; stresses that the promise-breaker profits. Not just 'forgetting' a promise.
usage.zh: 贬义，强调失信者从中得利，不只是忘记承诺。

meaning.en: Chatter that never gets near anything serious or worthwhile.
meaning.zh: 谈话不涉及正经道理，只说些无聊的话。

examples.zh: 他们整天聚在一起言不及义，浪费时间。
examples.en: They gather every day for idle chatter and waste time.

examples.zh: 会议上大家言不及义，没有讨论出结果。
examples.en: At the meeting everyone chatted pointlessly and nothing was decided.

story.en: Confucius criticised those who gather all day and 'never say anything of substance, and love to show off small cleverness'.
story.zh: 子曰：“群居终日，言不及义，好行小慧，难矣哉！”

usage.en: Mildly critical of small talk or empty conversation; formal. Not an accusation of lying.
usage.zh: 略带批评，指闲谈无聊，不指说谎。

meaning.en: To remember something (usually a kindness) for the rest of one's life.
meaning.zh: 一辈子都不会忘记，多指感恩。

equivalents: never forget as long as I live

examples.zh: 你的大恩大德，我没齿难忘。
examples.en: I'll never forget your great kindness as long as I live.

examples.zh: 那次旅行的美好回忆，让我没齿难忘。
examples.en: The wonderful memories of that trip will stay with me forever.

usage.en: Used for gratitude and cherished memories; 没 is mò (to end), not méi. 没齿 means 'the end of life'.
usage.zh: 多用于感恩和美好回忆；“没”读 mò，“没齿”指终生。

meaning.en: Cups and dishes scattered everywhere after a feast; a messy table.
meaning.zh: 杯子和盘子乱七八糟，形容宴会过后的凌乱景象。

examples.zh: 聚会结束后，桌上杯盘狼藉。
examples.en: After the party, the table was a mess of dirty cups and plates.

examples.zh: 看着杯盘狼藉的厨房，他叹了口气。
examples.en: Looking at the kitchen with dishes strewn about, he sighed.

story.en: Chunyu Kun describes a late feast where 'cups and dishes are in disorder' (杯盘狼藉) and he is most delighted.
story.zh: 淳于髡说酒阑席散时“杯盘狼藉，堂上烛灭”。

usage.en: Describes a scene after eating and drinking; 藉 is jí, not jiè. 狼藉 = messy, as wolves sleep on grass.
usage.zh: 形容吃喝之后的凌乱；“藉”读 jí。

meaning.en: An ideal son-in-law, someone any parent would be proud to have.
meaning.zh: 称心如意的好女婿。

equivalents: a fine catch for a daughter

examples.zh: 王家得了个乘龙快婿，逢人就夸。
examples.en: The Wangs got an ideal son-in-law and praise him to everyone.

examples.zh: 这位年轻医生一表人才，是不少人眼中的乘龙快婿。
examples.en: The handsome young doctor is seen by many as an ideal son-in-law.

usage.en: Positive, formal; about a daughter's husband only, not a general term for talented men.
usage.zh: 褒义，仅指女婿，不泛指有才之人。

meaning.en: The ox-headed and horse-faced guards of the underworld; used of ugly, villainous people.
meaning.zh: 传说中阴间的两个鬼卒，比喻面目丑恶的坏人。

examples.zh: 一帮牛头马面的家伙堵在门口。
examples.en: A gang of hideous thugs was blocking the door.

examples.zh: 戏里的牛头马面把观众吓了一跳。
examples.en: The ox-head and horse-face in the play gave the audience a fright.

usage.en: Derogatory, often humorous or figurative; refers to the underworld guards of folk belief.
usage.zh: 贬义，常带诙谐，源于民间传说中的阴间鬼差。

meaning.en: To read very fast, taking in ten lines at a glance; sometimes with the hint of skimming.
meaning.zh: 一眼就能看十行文字，形容读书速度很快。

examples.zh: 她读书一目十行，一个晚上就读完了这本书。
examples.en: She reads at lightning speed and finished the book in one evening.

examples.zh: 一目十行容易漏掉细节，重要文件要细读。
examples.en: Skimming can miss details, so read important documents carefully.

story.en: The Liang history says of Emperor Jianwen of Liang that when he read, his eyes took in ten lines at once (读书十行俱下).
story.zh: 《梁书》记梁简文帝“读书十行俱下”。

usage.en: Praise for quick reading, but may imply carelessness; note 行 is read háng (lines).
usage.zh: 多为赞扬，有时暗指不够仔细；“行”读 háng。

meaning.en: A scene in which all are silent and lifeless; a society stifled and without any voice.
meaning.zh: 千万匹马都不出声，比喻社会沉闷，无人敢说话，缺乏生气。

examples.zh: 万马齐喑的局面必须被打破。
examples.en: The deadly silence must be broken.

examples.zh: 没有自由讨论的社会，难免万马齐喑。
examples.en: A society without free discussion is bound to fall silent.

story.en: Gong Zizhen lamented: 'Only wind and thunder can bring life to China, yet ten thousand horses all stand mute, a grievous thing.'
story.zh: “九州生气恃风雷，万马齐喑究可哀。”

usage.en: Literary; often used for the political or intellectual atmosphere. 喑 is yīn, mute.
usage.zh: 书面语，常用于形容政治或思想领域的沉闷；“喑”读 yīn。

meaning.en: To pass on the wisdom of the ancients without inventing anything oneself; a modest scholarly attitude.
meaning.zh: 只阐述前人的学说，而不自己创作，是一种谦逊的治学态度。

examples.zh: 孔子自称述而不作，信而好古。
examples.en: Confucius said he transmitted rather than created, trusting and loving antiquity.

examples.zh: 他述而不作，把古籍整理得清清楚楚。
examples.en: He transmitted rather than created, putting the old books in perfect order.

story.en: Confucius said: 'I transmit but do not create; I believe in and love the ancients.'
story.zh: 子曰：“述而不作，信而好古，窃比于我老彭。”

usage.en: Literary and modest; often in discussing scholars. Not a criticism of lacking creativity.
usage.zh: 书面语，谦逊的说法，并非批评缺乏创意。

meaning.en: Of advanced age and high moral standing.
meaning.zh: 年纪大，品德高尚，多形容受人尊敬的长者。

examples.zh: 他是村里年高德劭的老先生，大家都听他的。
examples.en: He is the village's venerable elder and everyone listens to him.

examples.zh: 请年高德劭的前辈来主持这个仪式。
examples.en: We invited a respected elder to preside at the ceremony.

usage.en: Respectful, formal; applies to elders. 劭 is shào (not shāo).
usage.zh: 敬称长者；“劭”读 shào。

meaning.en: To strengthen the defences and remove everything useful from the fields, leaving the enemy no supplies.
meaning.zh: 加固防御，并把野外的粮食、物资转移或销毁，使敌人无所掠取。

examples.zh: 守军采取坚壁清野的办法，拖垮了敌军。
examples.en: The defenders wore the enemy down by fortifying the walls and stripping the land.

examples.zh: 面对强敌，他主张坚壁清野，固守待援。
examples.en: Facing a strong foe, he urged a scorched-earth defence and holding on for relief.

story.en: Xun Yu advised Cao Cao to hold fast and 'strengthen the walls and clear the fields' to await the enemy.
story.zh: 荀彧：“若……坚壁清野以待之。”

usage.en: Military term, neutral; 'scorched earth' only roughly; focuses on denying supplies. Also figurative in business.
usage.zh: 军事用语；主要指使敌人得不到补给，也可比喻商战。

meaning.en: To give a secret, flirtatious glance; or, figuratively, to make covert overtures to win someone's favour.
meaning.zh: 暗中递送含情的眼色；比喻暗中向人表示好意以求讨好。

examples.zh: 她对着他暗送秋波。
examples.en: She cast a flirtatious glance at him.

examples.zh: 这家公司向对手暗送秋波，想谈合作。
examples.en: The company is quietly making overtures to its rival to discuss cooperation.

usage.en: Playful, sometimes ironic; 秋波 is a metaphor for the eyes. Figurative use is often about politics or business.
usage.zh: 带调侃，“秋波”喻眼神；比喻义多用于政治、商业。

natural: glib words and an ingratiating look

meaning.en: Smooth words and a pleasing face used to win favour; insincere flattery.
meaning.zh: 花言巧语，装出和善的脸色，以取悦别人。

examples.zh: 巧言令色之徒，往往不可信。
examples.en: Those with glib tongues and false charm are often untrustworthy.

examples.zh: 他巧言令色，骗取了不少人的信任。
examples.en: He won many people's trust with smooth talk and a charming face.

story.en: Confucius: 'Clever words and a flattering look are seldom signs of humaneness.'

usage.en: Derogatory; usually of someone seeking favour; also in Confucius's famous remark. Often with 鲜矣仁.
usage.zh: 贬义，指谄媚取悦者，常引孔子名言。

natural: itch at the sight of the hunt

meaning.en: To be thrilled at seeing something one used to enjoy, and long to take it up again.
meaning.zh: 看到别人打猎，自己也高兴起来，比喻旧时爱好一旦触及，便又产生兴趣。

equivalents: be tempted to take up a pastime again

examples.zh: 看到比赛，他见猎心喜，也想上场。
examples.en: Watching the match, he felt the old itch and wanted to play.

examples.zh: 老摄影师见猎心喜，又拿起了相机。
examples.en: The old photographer felt the pull and picked up his camera again.

usage.en: Playful; of old hobbies. Not necessarily about hunting. Mildly self-mocking.
usage.zh: 略带自嘲，多指旧爱好。

meaning.en: To stand aloof from worldly concerns and not be attached to them.
meaning.zh: 置身于世俗事务之外，不受牵累。

examples.zh: 他隐居山中，超然物外。
examples.en: He lives in seclusion in the mountains, above worldly concerns.

examples.zh: 面对名利，她始终超然物外。
examples.en: She has always stayed aloof from fame and profit.

usage.en: Positive, literary; can also mean aloof or indifferent to an ongoing dispute (when criticising).
usage.zh: 褒义，书面语；有时也指置身事外。

synonyms: 别人笑我太疯癫，我笑他人看不穿

meaning.en: Stately, solemn music or writing; the great bell and pitch pipe of ancient ritual music.
meaning.zh: 古代音乐的两种乐律，形容音乐或言辞庄严、正大、高妙。

examples.zh: 这支乐曲庄重宏大，如黄钟大吕。
examples.en: This piece is solemn and grand, like the great bell and pipe.

examples.zh: 他的发言有黄钟大吕之声，引人深思。
examples.en: His speech had a stately ring and made people think.

usage.en: Literary praise for dignified music or style. 吕 is lǚ, not lǘ. The opposite of 靡靡之音.
usage.zh: 书面语，赞美庄重的音乐或文辞；“吕”读 lǚ。

natural: skilled in both statecraft and war

meaning.en: Mastery of both civil governance and military strategy.
meaning.zh: 文才武略兼备，指在治国和用兵方面都很有谋略。

equivalents: skilled in both statecraft and warfare

examples.zh: 诸葛亮文韬武略，辅佐刘备三分天下。
examples.en: Zhuge Liang was a master of statecraft and war, helping Liu Bei to carve out a third of the realm.

examples.zh: 他是个文韬武略的全才。
examples.en: He is an all-rounder in both civil and military matters.

usage.en: Praise for leaders and commanders; also humorously for all-round talent. 略 is lüè.
usage.zh: 褒义，赞美统帅、领袖，也可戏称全才；“略”读 lüè。

meaning.en: Great ability to manage the affairs of the realm.
meaning.zh: 以天地为经纬，形容具有治理天下的雄才大略。

examples.zh: 他是个经天纬地之才，可惜生不逢时。
examples.en: He was a man of world-shaping talent, but born at the wrong time.

examples.zh: 她有经天纬地的抱负。
examples.en: She has the ambition to reshape the world.

story.en: The Zuo Zhuan says that one who 'weaves heaven and earth' is called literate (经纬天地曰文).

usage.en: Highly complimentary, literary; used for statesmen and great minds.
usage.zh: 评价极高，书面语，多用于政治家、大才。

meaning.en: A broad and open road; a clear path to success. Often contrasted with 独木桥.
meaning.zh: 通往西域的大路，比喻宽广光明的道路。

examples.zh: 人家走阳关大道，我们只能过独木桥。
examples.en: They take the broad highway, while we can only cross a single-log bridge.

examples.zh: 改革为企业打开了一条阳关大道。
examples.en: Reform has opened up a broad road for the company.

usage.en: Positive; often with 独木桥 in the saying 你走你的阳关道，我过我的独木桥. Sometimes confused with 康庄大道.
usage.zh: 褒义，常与“独木桥”并用。

meaning.en: Nothing is worse (or more extreme) than this; used to stress the extreme degree of something.
meaning.zh: 没有比这更严重的了。

examples.zh: 浪费粮食之严重，莫此为甚。
examples.en: Nothing is more serious than this waste of food.

examples.zh: 对师长不敬，莫此为甚。
examples.en: There is no greater disrespect to one's teachers than this.

usage.en: Formal; used mostly for criticism, though can be neutral. 甚 is shèn. Often in 为害/为患莫此为甚.
usage.zh: 书面语，多用于批评，也可中性。

meaning.en: A person who is well dressed but behaves like an animal; a scoundrel.
meaning.zh: 穿着衣帽的禽兽，比喻品行恶劣、行为如同禽兽的人。

equivalents: a scoundrel with a respectable front

examples.zh: 这个衣冠禽兽，竟然欺骗了那么多老人。
examples.en: That scoundrel in a respectable suit deceived so many old people.

examples.zh: 别被他的外表骗了，他是个衣冠禽兽。
examples.en: Don't be fooled by his looks; he is a wolf in sheep's clothing.

usage.en: Strongly derogatory; of men with a respectable outside.
usage.zh: 贬义极强，用于外表体面、行为恶劣的人。
